title: Common free-chart section comparisons for a split module sequence
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ a short complex of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume $A,C$ finite locally free of ranks $r,s$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $U$ be open with a splitting $e:B|_U\simeq A|_U\oplus C|_U$ such that $ef=\mathrm{inl}$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2e=g$. Exterior sheaves are the sheafifications of algebraic exterior powers [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Every $x\in U$ admits $x\in V\subseteq U$ such that, on every $W\subseteq V$, there are bases of $A(W),C(W)$ indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(r),\mathrm{Fin}(s)$ and a linear equivalence $e_W:B(W)\simeq A(W)\times C(W)$ with $e_W(f_W(a))=(a,0)$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2e_W=g_W$. The sheafification unit $\bigwedge^{r+s}B(W)\to(\bigwedge^{r+s}B)(W)$ is bijective. So is the composite from $\bigwedge^r A(W)\otimes\bigwedge^s C(W)$ to $(\bigwedge^r A\otimes\bigwedge^s C)(W)$ of the tensor of the two exterior sheafification units and the canonical tensorSectionsMap. No lift function or determinant map is assumed.

proof.text: Use isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff_exists_over_iso_free and the covering property to choose trivializing opens for A and C containing x. Intersect these opens with U, obtaining V. Restrict each frame to V by restrictCompIso, restrictFreeIso and overIsoFreeEquiv. Transport the given splitting through overEquiv U, overFunctorEquiv U and the binary biproduct comparison, checking the two equations by faithfulness and naturality. Evaluate it at Over.mk(W to U), compose the evaluation biproduct comparison with ModuleCat.biprodIsoProd, and evaluate the two equations to obtain eW and its formulas. The outside section bases are Pi.basisFun transported by sectionsLinearEquivOfIsoFree and reindexed using Equiv.ulift. Restrict the over-site splitting to V by overMap and overFunctorMap; this restriction preserves binary coproducts and zero morphisms, hence binary biproducts. Compose with the two frames, biprod.isoCoprod, freeSumIso and the sum-index equivalence to obtain a middle frame indexed by ULift(Fin(r+s)).

Apply exteriorSheaf_local_free_comparison to the middle frame and the two outside frames. The second conclusions give bijectivity on every W inside V of the middle exterior unit and both outside exterior units. Apply the first conclusion only to C with degree s. The type of s-element subsets of Fin s is a singleton, since a subset with s elements is all of Fin s. Thus freeUniqueIso identifies the third top exterior sheaf over V with the unit, and exists_isFreeGenerator_of_iso supplies its free generator t. This includes s=0, and does not require a nonzero ring.

For every W inside V, the restriction of t is a free generator. TensorProduct.bijective_tmul_right_of_bijective_smul gives bijectivity of the algebraic map z to z tensor t restricted to W, and IsFreeGenerator.bijective_tmulSection_right gives bijectivity of the sheaf tensor map z to tmulSection z t restricted to W. The latter is definitionally the composite of tensorSectionsMap with the former. Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff therefore proves bijectivity of tensorSectionsMap. TensorProduct.map_bijective applied to the two exterior units proves bijectivity of their tensor map. Compose these bijections to obtain the asserted tensor comparison. The argument uses no positivity or nonzero-ring assumption and covers rank zero and empty opens.

The tensor comparison needs a generator of the third top exterior sheaf only; no wedge generator of the first term is needed. All private helpers are proved. lean.statement:
theorem determinant_split_chart_comparison {X : Scheme.{v}}
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (r s : ℕ)
    [S.X₁.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank r] [S.X₃.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank s]
    (U : X.Opens)
    (e : S.X₂.restrict U.ι ≅ S.X₁.restrict U.ι ⊞ S.X₃.restrict U.ι)
    (hf : (restrictFunctor U.ι).map S.f ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl)
    (hg : e.hom ≫ biprod.snd = (restrictFunctor U.ι).map S.g) :
    ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U), x ∈ V ∧
      ∀ (W : X.Opens), W ≤ V →
        ∃ (a : Module.Basis (Fin r) (X.presheaf.obj (op W)) (S.X₁.val.obj (op W)))
          (c : Module.Basis (Fin s) (X.presheaf.obj (op W)) (S.X₃.val.obj (op W)))
          (eW : S.X₂.val.obj (op W) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.obj (op W)]
            (S.X₁.val.obj (op W) × S.X₃.val.obj (op W))),
          (∀ z, eW (S.f.val.app (op W) z) = (z, 0)) ∧
          (∀ z, (eW z).2 = S.g.val.app (op W) z) ∧
          Function.Bijective
            (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app
              ((S.X₂.val.exteriorPower (R := X.presheaf) (r + s)))).app (op W)) ∧
          Function.Bijective
            ((tensorSectionsMap (exteriorPower S.X₁ r) (exteriorPower S.X₃ s) W).comp
              (TensorProduct.map (R := X.presheaf.obj (op W))
                (R₂ := X.presheaf.obj (op W)) (σ₁₂ := RingHom.id _)
                (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
                  (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app
                  (S.X₁.val.exteriorPower (R := X.presheaf) r)).app (op W)).hom
                (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
                  (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app
                  (S.X₃.val.exteriorPower (R := X.presheaf) s)).app (op W)).hom))
